title: Oncall handoff notes - Cameron Evans (night)
content:
Shift: 2024-11-02 night (18:00-06:00 UTC)
Owner: Cameron Evans
Primary contact: Priya Menon (pager)
Backup: Noah Thompson

Quick summary:
- Quiet start, but saw a couple of transient 500 spikes on hosted-api around 19:10 UTC. Lasted ~7m and recovered. Appears correlated with a deploy to hosted-api staging that bubbled into canary in region-us-west.
- Redis write latency flapped on cache-cluster-03 (pod restarts). Put a temp mitigation in place: failover to replica, increased pod restart backoff, created ticket SRE-987.
- No open Sev incidents at handoff time.

What to watch for next shift:
- hosted-api 95th p95 latency for token-generation route (/v1/generate). Threshold alerts at 800ms. We saw p95 ~920ms during the spike. If you see repeated p95 > 1s for >10m, follow "API latency escalation" below.
- Cache-cluster-03: monitor redis rejected-conns and ReplicaLag. If replica lag > 2s for >5m, consider manual failover.
- Autoscaler for dedicated pool dp-prod-gpu: check pending pods queue and GPU utilization. Scale-up automation has been flaky after morning maintenance.

Open items / ongoing investigations:
- SRE-987 (Redis flapping): root cause likely a noisy GC on node ip-10-2-11 causing kubelet OOM kills; need to confirm with kernel logs. Assigned Priya.
- INC-4321 (Model fallback misroute): some requests routed to quantized-2b variant unexpectedly. Hypothesis: routing policy fallback table got updated during a config push. PR: github.com/redwood/routing/pull/412 (in review).

Temporary procedures (for this shift) - quick copyable steps:
1) If hosted-api p95 > 1s for > 10m:
  - First: Check incident dashboard -> hosted-api -> p95 chart -> timeframe.
  - Second: Check canary status (console/rollouts) for any recent canary flips in the last 30m. If canary is in-progress, pause rollouts and roll back canary version.
  - Third: If cannot identify canary, temporarily route traffic to fallback model alias (model: text-davinci-2b-fallback) via feature-flag in routing service: POST /admin/routing/override (auth: SRE-bot).
  - Note: This is a temporary mitigation; notify product and apm-team in Slack and create a short incident note.

2) Redis node restart loop (cache-cluster-03):
  - Check pod restarts: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=redis-cache-cluster-03 -o wide.
  - If restarts > 3 in 15m, cordon node, drain, and failover to replica: redis-cli --cluster failover (follow our automated playbook).
  - If node OOM suspected, increase restartBackoff to 60s in k8s deployment for noisy node while investigating.
  - Create PR to bump liveness probe thresholds (SRE-987) and link to ticket.

3) Model fallback/route mismatch (INC-4321):
  - Check routing config history: git log on routing repo for last 24h, grep for fallback-table or policy changes.
  - Re-apply known-good policy: kubectl apply -f /configs/routing/policy-stable.yaml (run in staging first).
  - If traffic already affected, temporarily pin customers to model-version via per-customer override in the admin console.

Escalation contacts (order):
- Priya Menon (pager) - primary SRE
- Noah Thompson (pager) - secondary
- Maya Singh (on-call infra-engineer) - for infra/GPU issues
- Oncall-sre rotation Slack channel (#oncall-night-rotation) - use for >30m outages

Notes to next shift (open tasks):
- Follow up on SRE-987: confirm kernel logs for ip-10-2-11, attach output to ticket and decide on host reprovisioning.
- Verify that the routing PR (#412) either gets reverted or rolled forward with tests passing.
- Add a short smoke test to verify no unexpected fallback behavior when rolling canaries (small script in repo: tools/routing-smoke-test).

Scratchpad / quick commands:
- kubectl -n hosted logs deploy/hosted-api -c api --since=20m | grep ERROR
- curl -sS https://metrics.redwood/api/v1/query?query=p95_hosted_api | jq .
- redis-cli -h cache-cluster-03.monitor get top_keys_sample
- git -C /srv/routing show --name-only HEAD~5..HEAD

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Is there an automatic rollback threshold for canary when p95 breaches? Current behavior: some rollouts continue despite minor p95 blips; we should confirm desired policy. (Raised as note to product/console-and-rollouts).
- Confirm whether the autoscaler uses new GPU utilization metric (gpu_util_v2) or legacy metric. If legacy, we should transition to v2 to avoid missed scale-ups.

Attachments / links:
- INC-4321: https://jira.redwood.example/browse/INC-4321
- SRE-987: https://jira.redwood.example/browse/SRE-987
- Routing PR: https://github.com/redwood/routing/pull/412
- Runbook (prod failover): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/SRE/Production+Failover+Runbook

TODOs for next oncall:
- Re-run redis reproduce script on ip-10-2-11 (script lives in infra/redis/repro.sh)
- Add the smoke test above to CI (quick patch, low risk)
- Sweep recent deploys for any config pushes to routing table (grep deploy logs)

Final notes:
- Keep phone on silent but monitor pager. Night shifts usually calm but the cache flapping has been intermittent; if you get a page for cache-cluster-03, treat as high priority.
- I left a short snippet in my personal notes with kernel dmesg around the restart time (attached to SRE-987).

End of handoff.

-- Cameron
